story: In September 2025, eight pregnant women died at a public hospital in Agadir. The deaths set off Morocco's largest protests in years, led by a leaderless online movement calling itself GenZ 212, whose chant, "We want hospitals, not just stadiums," hit at a government spending billions on the 2030 World Cup. The protesters appealed directly to King Mohammed VI and demanded that Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch, a billionaire businessman, resign (KAS). A year later, Moroccans got their answer at the ballot box, in a way.

In the 23 September election, Akhannouch's RNI fell to 66 seats. Its coalition partner, the Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM), came first with 97, boosted by recruiting Fouzi Lekjaa, the head of the football federation, weeks before the vote (Reuters via TimesLive). Turnout was just 38 percent, the lowest since 2007, a sign that many young people still do not see elections as the place where change happens (Kuwait Times). On 29 September, the king appointed PAM's Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, a lawyer and former Marrakech mayor, as Morocco's first woman head of government. Her government will oversee the last stretch of a $20 billion World Cup build-out, the same spending the protesters questioned.
briefing.power: A constitutional monarchy where the king holds most real power, controlling defence, foreign affairs, religion and security. He must appoint the head of government from the party that wins most seats in the 395-seat House of Representatives, and the government handles domestic policy.
briefing.holders: King Mohammed VI; Head of Government Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri (PAM), appointed September 2026.
